newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline firm on NYMEX unleaded gains, run cuts.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline firm on NYMEX unleaded gains, run cuts.

text.p: NWE gasoline strengthened on Thursday as sharp gains in NYMEX unleaded futures propelled prices higher, traders said.
NYMEX June unleaded futures were trading 0.42 cent higher at 66.95 cents a gallon at 1725 GMT having posted a 1.14-cent gain on Wednesday.
Traders said the gains had unblocked the price stalemate which stalled trade on Wednesday.
Eurograde barges traded at $210 fob Rotterdam for first-half June early on, and then were done twice at $210 and once at $210.50 fob Rotterdam for pre end-May delivery.
Regular barges traded at $201.50 and $202.50 fob Rotterdam for balance of May.
News that BP had cut crude runs at the Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam due to poor margins had also firmed prices.

Sources familiar with the refinery said BP cut runs by 10 percent for the month of May as of midnight on Wednesday, equivalent to a 40 percent cut for the balance of May. BP controls 65 percent of the refinery.
Last week, Texaco, which controls 35 percent of the refinery, cut runs by the equivalent of 20 percent for the second half of May.
Other refiners in the region were said to monitoring the situation closely.
On the cargo front, traders said prices remained strong.

Traders said healthy U.S. demand and a dearth of U.K. cargoes, as local players held onto material in the expectation of a tax hike on auto fuel in the Labour government's post-election mini budget, were keeping prices buoyant.
"It's simply not that easy to find cargoes," one trader said.
There was talk that some players might be trying to build cargoes out of barge material.
